notes: Diagnostic only: production four ACK buffers, one-quantum offload floor and 4 MiB/s control limit. No scheduling, clock, packing or buffer-policy change.

Fresh versus retained requests are counted once at successful Flight.prepare. Retained means Batch.head is nonzero. Permit histograms count DATA grants received at the worker, including ones later expired/canceled; probes are excluded. Bins count requests/grants with 1, 2-4, 5-8, 9-16, 17-32, 33-64 physical datagrams.

Short-pending counts fully successful DATA grants of at most 16 datagrams with nonempty same-lane pending FIFO. Short-tail-pending is its subset that consumes the entire remaining retained plan. Existing unsent frame handles already in a batch but outside its plan do not count as pending FIFO, so this is a conservative backlog signal.

Byte totals include outer IPv6/UDP headers. Counter totals include drain. The extra local counter writes and bounded sums add diagnostic overhead; use these distributions for attribution, not as an exact production goodput baseline.

340 ordinary release tests, 15 sender kernel regressions, all-target/all-feature musl Clippy, fmt and diff checks pass. Histogram boundaries, fresh/retained separation, worker/session totals and wire-byte consistency have assertions.

Four retained-daemon 20-second points; builds and other tests stopped during load. All points have zero outer fragmentation, socket errors/overflow, inner UDP errors, admission pressure and receiver invalid/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run/reordered records.
Short retained tails are a measured scheduling cost opportunity; no refill throughput gain is established by this diagnostic. Neither target or CPU ceiling is established.
